title: Private Deploy Commissioning and Safety Gate Playbook
author: Arjun Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook describes the commissioning and safety-gate process for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It consolidates the preflight conformance checks, packaging/attestation requirements, day-2 validation, upgrade & rollback decision criteria, and customer sign-off gates into a single operator-facing guide. Use this document to run acceptance dry-runs, provide deterministic go/no-go signals for rollouts, and capture evidence bundles for compliance reviews.

Scope:
- Applies to new private deployments (VPC and air-gapped on-prem).
- Covers: pre-install validation, initial commissioning, nightly/first-week day-2 checks, controlled upgrade decision gates, rollback triggers, and evidence collection for customers/regulators.
- Excludes tenant-level application testing (customer responsibility), but includes tenant-impacting safety checks.

Owner and contact:
- Playbook owner: eng-private-deployments (operator lead: Arjun Patel).
- Primary oncall (field ops): rotation in PagerDuty schedule "private-field-ops".
- Escalation: SRE pager -> Platform eng -> Product security.

Quick summary of safety gates (high-level):
1) Preflight PASS required: hardware attestation, network topology, and KMS handshake.
2) Install PASS required: control-plane services green, model runtime health >= 99.5% in synthetic workload.
3) Day-2 PASS required before enabling tenant burst: KV-consistency checks, prefix-cache integrity, and SLO smoke tests.
4) Upgrade gate: evidence of no-regression on guarded prompt-sets and telemetry baselining.
5) Rollback gate: defined and rehearsed steps with snapshot evidence and customer communication templates.

Preflight checklist (operator):
- Documentation: delivery manifest, customer contact, accepted network CIDR and egress policy.
- Hardware: motherboard/CPU firmware versions, NIC driver versions, TPM/HSM presence, and disk encryption.
- Network: BGP/PEER config validated, required ports open (see table), connectivity test to control-plane endpoints.
- KMS: asymmetric auth path established, test encrypt/decrypt with sample key.
- Images & artifacts: signed images present and verified against attestation key.
- Time sync: NTP within 50ms of stratum source.

Ports and endpoints (minimum required):
| Purpose                     | Protocol/Port | Example endpoint                         | Notes                                      |
|-----------------------------|---------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Control-plane API           | HTTPS/443     | control.redwood.example.net              | TLS cert signed by Redwood CA or customer  |
| Telemetry (metrics)         | TCP/9091      | telemetry.internal.local                 | mTLS required                              |
| Model runtime gRPC          | TCP/7070      | runtime-node.local                       | Internal-only via service mesh             |
| KV sync / snapshot          | TCP/8200      | storage.local                            | Encrypted, authenticated                   |

Hardware & packaging attestation requirements:
- Image signing: SHA256 signature verified by operator CLI (example: redwood-signer verify image.tar.gz.sig).
- Firmware inventory: record vendor, serial, BIOS/firmware version.
- TPM/HSM: attest nonce exchange and record certificate.
- Package manifest example (YAML) to include in evidence bundle (operator should run):

# Example manifest (YAML)
# operator: run `redwood-manifest collect --output manifest.yml`

operator: redwood-field
customer: example-corp
nodes:
  - hostname: node-01
    serial: ABC123
    bios: 1.2.3
  - hostname: node-02
    serial: DEF456
    bios: 1.2.3
images:
  runtime: registry.redwood/v1/runtime:2026-01-10
  tools: registry.redwood/v1/tools:2026-01-10
signatures:
  runtime: runtime.sig
  tools: tools.sig

Pre-install commands (smoke):
1) Verify control-plane reachability:
   curl -sS -D - https://control.redwood.example.net/health | grep "OK"
2) KMS handshake test (example):
   redwood-kms-cli encrypt --key <key-id> --plaintext "preflight" --out /tmp/preflight.enc && redwood-kms-cli decrypt --key <key-id> --in /tmp/preflight.enc
3) Image signature verification:
   redwood-signer verify registry.redwood/v1/runtime:2026-01-10 --sig runtime.sig

Install & commissioning steps (numbered):
1) Operator performs node provisioning and boots to recovery image.
2) Run manifest collection: `redwood-manifest collect --output manifest.yml` and attach to ticket.
3) Install runtime images via signed artifact installer: `installer apply --manifest manifest.yml`
4) Start control-plane services behind canary routing: bring up minimal control-plane (api, auth, telemetry).
5) Run fast integration test (10 minute synthetic):
   - 10min synthetic workload with 50 qps, sequence length distribution matching customer profile.
   - Monitor model runtime for OOM, stalls, and CPU steal.
6) If synthetic hit errors >1% or p50 latency > customer SLO + 25% => FAIL -> revert to snapshot and file RCA.

First-week day-2 validation checklist (automated + manual):
- Nightly drift detection: config drift check vs manifest.
- KV-consistency sweep: run `kv-check --verify --window 24h`. Expected result: 0 mismatches.
- Prefix-cache integrity: run `cache-validate --prefix-samples file://sample-prefixes.json`.
- Latency smoke: run synthetic traces at 1% of expected production qps with representative prompts. Record p50/p95.
- Telemetry retention sanity: ensure metrics are ingested and retained for minimum 7 days (operator internal policy).

Telemetry & evidence matrix (table for compliance):
| Evidence artifact                | Required for acceptance | Storage location example                  | Retention |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-----------|
| manifest.yml                     | yes                      | s3://evidence/private-deploys/<id>/manifest | 1 year    |
| attestation certs                | yes                      | s3://evidence/.../attestations            | 7 years   |
| synthetic workload report (csv)  | yes                      | s3://evidence/.../workloads               | 90 days   |
| preflight command outputs        | yes                      | s3://evidence/.../preflight               | 90 days   |

Upgrade decision gate (operator checklist):
- Inputs required: new image manifests, model signature, guarded prompt-set results from canary, telemetry baseline comparison, customer blackout windows.
- Run canary waveform: deploy new model variant to 2 nodes in limited tenant or internal test tenant.
- Run guarded prompt set (1000 prompts) and check for quality regression: failure if >1.5% drop in BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim threshold as defined per model family.
- Compare cost/latency telemetry: p95 must not exceed baseline p95 + 15% for steady load.
- If canary passes, perform staged rollout with automated pause points at 10%, 30%, 60%, 100% traffic. At each pause point run smoke suite (5 minute synthetic).

Rollback trigger matrix (examples):
- Safety-critical failure -> immediate rollback: control-plane auth failures, KV corruption detected, model producing toxic outputs flagged by safety pipeline.
- Performance regression -> conditional rollback if sustained for >15 minutes and p95 > baseline p95 + 25%.
- Resource exhaustion (OOM or GPU thermal shutdown) -> immediate rollback.

Rollback procedure (rehearsed steps):
1) Notify stakeholders using standard customer communication template (appendix B).
2) Activate runbook: `operator-rollback --deployment <id> --target-image <previous-image>` (this command orchestrates model swap and node-level rollback).
3) Validate rollback by running 5 minute synthetic workload and verifying SLOs.
4) Collect evidence bundle and file RCA ticket.

Customer-facing acceptance (signoff flow):
1) Operator complete acceptance bundle (manifest, attestations, synthetic reports, telemetry snapshot).
2) Share evidence link and schedule 1-hour review with customer security/infra contacts.
3) If customer raises concerns, escalate to eng-product for remediation plan.
4) Customer signs acceptance form (template in Appendix A) or requests remediation.

Automation and CI integration pointers:
- Preflight checks are implemented as a Jenkins/GitHub Actions job (job: private-deploy/preflight-check). Provide job URL in ticket for audit.
- Nightly drift detection runs from the platform pipeline (cron). Alerts create a Jira ticket with severity based on number of drifted nodes.

Operational runbook references (links):
- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/tenant-bootstrapping-and-immutable-upgrade-playbook-2026
- KV cache consistency playbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-consistency-chaos-validation-and-rollback-matrix-2028
- Packaging and attestation: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/model-artifact-supplychain-and-image-attestation-spec-2026

Risk register (top items and mitigations):
- Risk: KMS integration failure -> Mitigation: preflight handshake and fallback to operator-managed ephemeral key until resolved.
- Risk: Hidden firmware bugs -> Mitigation: firmware whitelist and short burn-in tests during provisioning.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps during initial week -> Mitigation: parallel ingestion to fallback collector and immediate retention in local evidence bucket.

Appendix A — Customer acceptance template (summary):
- Deployment ID: ______
- Date: ______
- Evidence link: ______
- Key tests run: preflight, synthetic workload, kv-consistency, prefix-cache validation
- Customer rep: ______ (name, email)
- Acceptance: [ ] Accepted  [ ] Remediate before acceptance

Appendix B — Communication templates (incident & rollback):
- Subject: [Redwood] Rollback initiated for private-deploy <id>
- Body: Short summary, impact, estimated time to remediation, contact details.

Appendix C — Example CLI snippets and troubleshooting hints:
- Collect manifest: `redwood-manifest collect --output manifest.yml`
- Run kv check: `kv-check --verify --window 24h --output kv-report.json`
- Verify image signature: `redwood-signer verify registry.redwood/v1/runtime:2026-01-10 --sig runtime.sig`
- Run synthetic workload: `redwood-synthetic --prompts sample-prompts.json --qps 50 --duration 600 --out report.csv`

Appendix D — Evidence collection checklist (operator fillable):
- [ ] manifest.yml uploaded
- [ ] attestation certs collected
- [ ] synthetic report attached
- [ ] preflight outputs attached
- [ ] canary results attached (if upgrade performed)

Notes and future improvements:
- Plan to integrate guarded prompt-set evaluation into the CI pipeline so canary validations produce signed attestations.
- Add automated customer-facing acceptance link generation to reduce manual handoff time.

If you find missing steps or want to add specific customer requirements, file a PR against this page and tag eng-private-deployments.
